verdict.label: Self-serve
verdict.summary: Linear OAuth2 apps are created instantly in your settings with no review process required.

composioFit.summary: Composio offers a managed OAuth app for Linear out of the box. You only need a custom app if you require your own branding, dedicated rate limits, or custom scopes.
whyOwnApp: Custom branding on the Linear consent screen
Custom scope configuration for targeted access permissions

phases.name: Create OAuth Application in Linear
steps: Log into Linear (preferably using a workspace created for application management).
Navigate to Settings > API > Applications > New (https://linear.app/settings/api/applications/new).
Enter your application name, description, and developer URL.
phases.handoff: App creation yields Client ID and Client Secret immediately.

phases.name: Configure Auth Config in Composio
steps: Create a new Auth Config for Linear in the Composio dashboard.
Copy the redirect URI provided by Composio.
Paste the redirect URI into the callback URLs setting of your Linear OAuth application.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from Linear back into Composio.
phases.handoff: Composio is now configured to execute OAuth flows with Linear.

phases.name: Test OAuth Authorization Flow
steps: Verify user consent flow and token exchange.
Confirm access token and refresh token generation.

artefacts.title: Linear OAuth Application Configuration
artefacts.body:
Application Name: My Agent Integration
Developer URL: https://yourdomain.com
Callback URLs: <Composio callback URL from your auth config>

artefacts.title: Linear Security & Privacy Guidelines
artefacts.body:
1. Store Client Secret securely within Composio.
2. Request minimal necessary scopes (e.g. read, write, or specific targeted scopes like issues:create).
3. Manage the application within a dedicated administrative workspace.

requirements.label: Configured Callback URL
requirements.when: Required when setting up the OAuth application in Linear settings.

requirements.label: Privacy Policy
requirements.when: Not strictly enforced for app creation, but standard for production applications.

scopes.purpose: Read access for the user's account (always present by default).
Write access for the user's account.
Allows creating and updating issues, and creating their attachments.
Full access to admin level endpoints.

redirectRules.rule: The redirect_uri passed to GET /oauth/authorize must match the callback URL configured in Linear application settings.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 400 or failed token exchange when requesting tokens.
blockers.cause: Sending the POST body to https://api.linear.app/oauth/token as JSON rather than form-urlencoded.

blockers.symptom: Authorization failure or redirect mismatch error during OAuth flow.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri query parameter does not exactly match the callback URL configured in Linear.
blockers.fix: Ensure the Composio callback URL is added verbatim to the Linear application callback URLs.
blockers.fallback: Check for protocol, domain, or slash mismatches in settings.

checklist.text: Create new OAuth application and enter details
Open Composio dashboard and create Linear custom auth config
Copy Composio redirect URI to Linear application callback URLs
Copy Client ID and Client Secret into Composio
Test OAuth integration flow and confirm token generation

uncertainties: Linear documentation does not specify any app review queue, user limits, or mandatory approval processes for production OAuth applications.

claims.text: Linear supports OAuth2 authentication for integrations.
claims.quote: Linear supports OAuth2 authentication, which is recommended if you’re building applications to integrate with Linear.

claims.text: OAuth applications can be created in Linear under API applications settings.
claims.quote: Create a new [OAuth2 Application](https://linear.app/settings/api/applications/new) and configure the redirect callback URLs to your application.

claims.text: It is recommended to manage the OAuth application in a dedicated workspace.
claims.quote: It is **highly recommended** you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

claims.text: Linear authorization endpoint is GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize.
Linear token endpoint is POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token.
Linear supports scopes including read, write, issues:create, comments:create, and admin.
claims.quote: * `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.

claims.text: The actor parameter configures whether resources are created as the authorizing user or the application.
claims.quote: * `user` - (Default) Resources are created as the user who authorized the application. This option should be used if you want each user to do their own authentication

claims.text: Actor app should be used for service accounts or agents.
claims.quote: * `app` - Resources are created as the application. This option should be used for agents and service accounts or agents.

claims.text: Linear supports the PKCE flow with code_challenge and code_challenge_method.
Linear access tokens are valid for 24 hours and must be refreshed using refresh tokens.
claims.quote: The access token is valid for 24 hours and will need to be refreshed when it expires.

claims.text: Token exchange requests must use application/x-www-form-urlencoded format.
claims.quote: Pass parameters in body as [URL-encoded form submission](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/POST#url-encoded_form_submission), where the `Content-Type` header must be `applicati

claims.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth application for Linear.
Custom auth configs can be created for custom branding, specific scopes, rate limits, or custom instances.
claims.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.

claims.text: Connecting a custom OAuth app requires copying the Composio redirect URI to the provider portal and copying Client ID and Secret back to Composio.
claims.quote: For OAuth toolkits, register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** back into Composio.

claims.text: Linear documentation does not define a mandatory app review or approval submission before production use.
claims.reason: Linear developer documentation provides instant application creation without mentioning a review process.
